name: Northern Corn Leaf Blight
affected_hosts: Primarily affects maize, but can also infect sorghum and sudangrass.
symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green lesions on leaves that turn tan
Lesions typically start on lower leaves and progress upwards
Leaf tissue death and premature senescence
conditions: Favored by cool to moderate temperatures (18-27C) and prolonged periods of leaf wetness (6-18 hours).
cycle: Spores are wind-dispersed from infected crop residue, germinate on wet leaves, and infect the plant, producing new spores within 1-2 weeks.
treatment: Fungicide application, especially during early disease development, can manage the disease.
diagnosis: Visual identification of characteristic lesions; laboratory isolation and identification of the pathogen can confirm.
impact: Significant yield losses (up to 50%) due to reduced photosynthetic area and premature plant death.
